To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PDIA is a promising approach to solving problems that are complex, wicked, and/or political.

1) PDIA can be a useful approach for development, and 2) it is important for PDIA to focus on locally nominated problems, encourage positive deviance and experiment, create feedback loops that facilitate learning, and engage multiple agents.

(a) PDIA is more effective than standard approaches to development because it promotes problem driven iterative adaptation, which (b) is more likely to produce positive change because it is less likely to lead to isomorphic mimicry, and (c) is less costly because it is more likely to avoid implementation failures and because it can be implemented at a lower budget.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make development work, and we propose an alternative way to do so.
how change actually happens in the real world.
the conditions under which development interventions produce intended effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PDIA is the best way to do development.
PDIA promotes a problem solving approach to development.
this article is about how to escape from capability traps through problem driven iterative adaptation (PDIA).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PDIA is about solving locally prioritized and nominated performance problems through iterative experimentation and rapid learning by multiple actors.
we have been trying to understand how change happens in development by conducting fine-grained qualitative analysis of development projects.
the most important factor in the success of development initiatives is the quality of problem-solving processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best way to improve development outcomes is to engage local actors in solving locally prioritized problems.
development is a process of solving problems.
development is about solving problems, not about transplanting best practices, and the best way to learn how to solve problems is by doing so.
